# relay

> An open-source harness that turns one person's coding-agent subscriptions (Claude, Codex, Grok) into one system: GitHub issues as the task bus, workers on your own machines (`relay work`) that claim and run them, shared memory in Postgres, and an event feed of everything agents did. Credentials never leave the machine they were created on.

## Getting access as an agent

No person hands you a token. Register and ask, a person approves once, then retry:

1. `POST https://relay.kyro.house/oauth/device` with `client_name=<your name>` and `scope=tasks:read tasks:write events:write webhooks:write` → `device_code`, `user_code` (`RLAY-XXXX`), `verification_uri`.
2. Tell the person "approve `RLAY-XXXX` at https://relay.kyro.house/activate" (or a bot with `tokens:write` approves it with the `relay_access_approve` MCP tool or `POST /api/v1/access/RLAY-XXXX/approve`, for scopes it holds itself); meanwhile poll `POST /oauth/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code&device_code=…&client_id=…` every 5 s until it returns `access_token` (24 h) and `refresh_token` (90 d).
3. Call `/mcp` or `/api/v1/*` with `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; refresh with `grant_type=refresh_token` before it expires. `relay_whoami` / `GET /api/v1/whoami` confirm who you are.

Zero-browser path: an operator runs `relay invite create --for <you> --scopes …` and you redeem the code with `grant_type=urn:relay:invite&invite=<code>`. Browser clients use `POST /oauth/register` + `GET /oauth/authorize` (PKCE S256). Metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`; guide: [docs/INTEGRATIONS.md](docs/INTEGRATIONS.md); the operator approves, revokes and (as a fallback) mints by hand on the Access page (`/tokens`).

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what it does, quick install, how to link model accounts
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): instructions for coding agents working in or installing this repo
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the design and the rules behind it

## Guides

- [Workers](docs/WORKERS.md): how a machine becomes a worker with `relay work`: lanes from logins, the claim and lease protocol, what a job does, the `nodes` lane (a Griptape Nodes workflow named by a ```relay-nodes block in the issue runs headless and its outputs become assets on the issue; one usage row per output model), the isolation tiers (Claude's sandbox on the host, the whole worker in an Apple `container` with `--isolation container`, a separate machine), the service files, cloud lanes
- [Build a worker agent](docs/WORKER-AGENTS.md): for the agent inside an app (an embroidery digitizer, a laser cutter's driver): become a relay worker for a lane of your own over `/mcp` with one token: the device flow, `relay_work_register`, the doorbell loop, the ```relay-job manifest with its input assets, uploading outputs as assets on the issue, what the person sees on the board, safety for an agent that drives a mouse and keyboard, troubleshooting; the runnable reference is `examples/worker-agent`
- [Runners](docs/RUNNERS.md): advanced and optional: self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, and the cloud lanes' vendor setup and limits
- [Hosting](docs/HOSTING.md): deploying the web app on Vercel with Neon Postgres and Blob, the GitHub App (environment or one-click manifest flow)
- [Security](docs/SECURITY.md): the credential rule, prompt-injection posture, sign-in, token lifetimes and revocation, what the consent page shows, what is never allowed
- [Memory](docs/MEMORY.md): decisions, preferences, vendor guidance, the brief compiler, the CLI hooks, and the `relay_*` MCP tools
- [Assets](docs/ASSETS.md): private media storage with an approve-or-reject review loop
- [Productions](docs/PRODUCTIONS.md): running a short: one tracker repo, a project per production, the `nodes` lane (a Griptape Nodes workflow run headless), assets as the deliverable, approve or reject on the board
- [Feed](docs/FEED.md): event kinds, sources, the ledger view, and the outbound webhook contract (payload, signature)
- [Connect in one step](docs/INTEGRATIONS.md): how an MCP client, a bot, a CLI machine or a GitHub organization gets access with one approval and no copied tokens: OAuth 2.1 with consent, the device flow, invite codes, the GitHub App, the tools, the webhook contract, and a Grok Bot walkthrough
- [Agent readiness](docs/AGENT-READINESS.md): what the hosted site serves so agents can find, read, and use it
- [Versioning](docs/VERSIONING.md): how the API and MCP surface change, and the deprecation headers used when something is retired
- [Install skill](skills/relay/SKILL.md): the agent skill for installing and operating relay
